unit.why: An exemplary tale about the pre-Hasidic R. Heschel of Krakow, who refused a bribe. It is quoted from Zera Berakh inside a halakhic discussion of bribery (שוחד) for judges.
unit.boundary_note: The division opens with item ב) of a series on bribery. It ends with a halakhic citation from the Tur/Beit Yosef that continues the topic. The next division begins a separate exemplum (R. Meir Gavizon).

stories.start_quote: אספרה מעשה אשר נעשה בימי הגמו״ר
stories.end_quote: לא המדרש עיקר אלא המעשה וכו'
stories.summary_en: A litigant gives R. Heschel of Krakow a hundred gold coins before a lawsuit. The rabbi gathers his sons and sons-in-law at a meal, counts the coins before them, and teaches them never to chase gifts as leaders, since he will return the money the next day rather than sell his soul.

tags.why: Praises the integrity of a pre-Hasidic rabbinic authority of Krakow; copied from Zera Berakh.

quotes: כדי שמעני תלמדו וכן תעשו שלא תהיו להוטים אחר מתנות
tags.why: The story is framed explicitly as a moral lesson against taking bribes.

quotes: ודבר זה נראה שאסור מצד שלבבו נוטה לדבר זה
tags.why: The tale is wrapped in a halakhic and ethical discussion of bribery.

quotes: וחלילה לי למכור נשמתי באלף אלפים אדומים זהב
אין אני נותן לאדוני בתורת שוחד
tags.why: The prohibition on bribery is the issue of the story.

quotes: שתיבת לאמתו מזהיר על שלא יצטרף הדיין
tags.why: The law on a judge's bias and on bribery is discussed.
A lawsuit before the rabbinical court is the setting.
His wife, sons and sons-in-law appear.
Rebbetzin Dina prepares the meal and is the oral source of the story.

quotes: אשר שמעתי מפיה של האלמנה הרבנית
tags.why: The story is framed as heard from the widow.
There is a festive meal with drinking, mentioned in passing.
